chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah who said:

I asked him about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And do not utter your Salat loudly nor be silent with it'. He said: 'The silent (khafitah) is what is less than what you can hear (yourself), and the loud (jahar) is that you raise your voice intensely'.

key_terms.الْجَهْرُ: Loudness; specifically referring to raising the voice intensely during recitation.
key_terms.الْمُخَافَتَةُ: The state of being silent or quiet; specifically referring to recitation volume below the level of one's own hearing.
key_terms.سَمْعِكَ: Your hearing; used here as the threshold for distinguishing between silent and audible recitation.
key_terms.قَوْلِ اللَّهِ: The Words of Allah; referring to the Quranic verse being interpreted.

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between silent and loud recitation in Islamic prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the middle path in recitation by defining 'khafat' (softness) as volume below one's own hearing and 'jahar' (loudness) as an intense, raising of the voice. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on moderation (wasatiyyah) in worship, ensuring the recitation is audible enough for self-reflection without becoming a distraction or showing off. This practical definition helps worshippers navigate the balance between internal contemplation and communal audibility.
